categories.intro: Rope Access technique of movement on a rope should only be used when traditional access systems cannot be installed. The basic rope access equipment should be used with a fall protection system. Rescue technique is used in an emergency hence it is naturally the most sensitive. This intervention can be performed by the user him/herself, if he/she is conscious and has the necessary equipment for selfextraction, or by a helper. In this situation it is necessary to be able to reach the victim, release him/her in complete safety and move the person upwards or downwards.

families.name: Full Body Harness (EN Standard, CE Marked)
families.intro: Our EN Standard Full Body Harnesses are developed for professional work-at-height applications where dependable fall protection and freedom of movement are essential. The range includes different harness configurations designed for applications such as fall arrest, work positioning, climbing, suspension, and rescue. Each model is engineered with durable webbing, secure attachment points, and adjustable components to support a stable and comfortable fit. Depending on the model, the range incorporates dorsal, sternal, lateral, and specialized rescue attachment points to suit specific working requirements.

families.name: Full Body Harness (BIS Standard, ISI Marked)
families.intro: Our BIS Standard Full Body Harnesses are built to provide dependable protection for workers operating at height. The range combines robust construction with practical design features to deliver a secure fit and reliable support throughout the workday. Designed for professional applications, these harnesses focus on ease of use, durability, and effective user protection. The range offers thoughtfully configured harness designs to accommodate different work environments and user requirements while complying with the applicable BIS safety standard.

families.name: Full Body Harness (ANSI Standard, ANSI Marked)
families.intro: Our ANSI Standard Full Body Harnesses are designed for professionals who require dependable fall protection and practical performance in demanding work environments. The range is developed with a focus on durability, secure attachment, and user comfort, making it suitable for a variety of work-at-height applications. With carefully engineered configurations and high-quality components, the ANSI range provides reliable support and a secure fit while allowing users to work with confidence. Different models are available to accommodate specific application and operational requirements.

families.name: Forked Lanyards with Energy Absorber
families.intro: Forked Lanyards allow the user easy movability at height, staying tied-off at all times for 100% fall protection. The Forked Lanyards are offered with a Shock Absorber to reduce the impact of jurk whenever any fall occurs. Forked Lanyards are made up of either Twisted Ropes, Kernmantle Ropes or 44mm wide high tenacity Polyester Webbing & Expandable Lanyards. Conforms to EN 355:2002.

families.name: Restraint Forked Lanyards
families.intro: Forked Restraint Lanyards (Twin Leg) come in Twisted Rope, Kernmantle Rope, 44mm wide polyester webbing & also available in Expandable Lanyard thereby offering the facility to move in all directions while remaining safely anchored at all times. The Lanyards are suited only for purpose of restraint, and should note be used for Fall protection since they do not have any Energy Absorber. Conforms to EN 354:2010

families.intro: S. B. FALL PROTECTION Fall Arrester & Temporary Anchorage Line Systems have a wide application of usage in fall arrest while climbing, and in restraint while working on roof tops, platforms and inclined planes.
bullets: In the event of a fall, they are designed to “grab” on to the Anchorage Line on which they move, thus arresting the fall immediately.
The Anchorage line, in conjunction with the given Rope Grab provides the necessary Shock Absorption.

families.name: Anchorages
families.intro: The Anchorage Point is commonly referred to as a secure tie off point. It is the place where a worker anchors himself so that he can easily move around that point, and also holds on safely, incase he experiences a fall.
bullets: According to EN 795:2012, Anchor Devices have been classified into various types, names Type A, B, C, D and E. SB FALL PROTECTION offers a range of anchor devices which fall under various such types.
